title: What We Learned From Day 1 of Formula E GEN4 Testing in Madrid
excerpt:
Catch up on all the action from Monday’s sessions at ABB FIA Formula E World Championship pre-season testing.

We are back! The ABB FIA Formula E World Championship took to the track at the Circuito de Madrid Jarama - RACE for the first day of pre-season testing on Monday with all 12 teams aiming to collect as much data as possible on the all-new GEN4 machinery.

As expected, some of the teams and drivers hit issues in the early stages of this brand new rules cycle, but there has been plenty to take away from the first day of action.

Formula E Pre-season Testing: Everything you need to know about GEN4 in Madrid

Here’s what we saw out on track as pre-season testing got underway.

GEN4 is rapid out of the box

The all-new GEN4 package has already delivered on its promise of being a far faster machine than the previous GEN3 Evo. Edoardo Mortara obliterated the fastest time from last season’s Madrid E-Prix with a chart-topping lap of 1 minute 24.344 seconds. Even at this early stage, the new cars have shown themselves to be more than five seconds quicker than previous machinery.

The cars are quick on the straights, too. On Mortara’s fastest lap, he was 25kph faster through the speed trap compared to FP1 last year, with a top speed of 277.2kph.

With two more days full of testing to go, there should be ample opportunity for the drivers to go even faster than we have already seen.

New (and old) liveries hit the track

With new cars and new teams come new colours! All 12 teams ventured out onto the circuit in their new GEN4 cars throughout Monday’s running.

Many teams have stuck with familiar paint schemes from previous seasons, while others have gone in a slightly different direction.

However, not every team has unveiled their colours for the upcoming season quite yet. Nissan is running with a black ‘404 Livery Not Found’ palette for the week.

Porsche works on race runs

Porsche started its afternoon session by focusing on race simulations, as part of gathering the data it needs for the season ahead. Reigning world champion Pascal Wehrlein and teammate Nico Muller both completed 15-lap runs at the start of the afternoon session with consistent lap times throughout.

This information allow the team to see how the car is performing in race trim in the very early stages of this new season. But, despite the long race runs, Porsche weren't the team to complete the most laps…

Citroen & Nissan produce the laps

Two of the busiest teams during the first full day of testing were Citroën and Nissan. While two-time Formula E champion Jean-Éric Vergne topped the times in the morning session, and Nick Cassidy also featured towards the top of the times, Citroen also completed the most laps of Jarama.

Nissan also completed a large number of laps. 2024/25 victor Oliver Rowland was among the busiest drivers during the day. His new teammate Zane Maloney not only completed a similar number of laps, but also featured towards the top of the times in both sessions.

Porsche and Jaguar powertrains completed the most laps, but Stellantis and Jaguar were not far behind.

Fortescue & Lola hit issues

Towards the lower end of the lap counts were Fortescue Zero and Lola. For Lola, running with two rookies this season, stoppages for both Robert Shwartzman and Enzo Fittipaldi impacted their run plans significantly.

Similarly, Dan Ticktum completed a limited number of laps with new team Fortescue Zero. However, all of the drivers got out and were able to gather some crucial information.

With plenty of track time still remaining across the week, both teams will be confident of building on those early baselines and quickly making up lost ground.

Only the beginning

All of the teams and drivers have a day away from track action on Tuesday, before they hit the Jarama circuit once again on Wednesday.

title: ‘Brilliant at the Basics’: Inside Fortescue Zero Racing’s Formula E Ambitions
excerpt:
Moving from the pit lane to the grid, Formula E’s Official PIT BOOST supplier Fortescue Zero has launched its own racing team, appointing Jim Wright as Team Principal.

After establishing itself as a key technical partner - delivering the battery technology behind Formula E’s ultra-fast 600 kW charging system that provides a 10% energy boost in under 30 seconds - Fortescue Zero Racing is now setting its sights on competing in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Only two months ago, Fortescue Zero announced its commitment to the Formula E's all-new GEN4 era, becoming the first Australian-owned team to join the grid. With the appointment of Jim Wright as Team Principal, the outfit has now completed another significant step in its preparations for its inaugural campaign.

"I'll prove the doubters wrong" - Dan Ticktum on finding a home at Fortescue for GEN4

For those who know motorsport, Wright needs little introduction. With decades of experience spanning Formula 1, Formula E and other international racing series, he has held senior positions at Williams F1, Scuderia Toro Rosso, Virgin Racing, Mahindra Racing, Venturi Formula E and Andretti Global. He also played a pivotal role in steering the Formula E Teams & Manufacturers Association throughout the championship’s first ten seasons.

Yet, despite an extensive career across the sport, the role of team principal marks a new chapter for Wright.

Speaking about what attracted him to the project, he explained: “When you have such a solid foundation, a multi-billion dollar company, profitable, committed to decarbonisation, committed to electrification, and a visionary like Andrew Forrest – it really is very easy to say, ‘well, look, that’s a very solid platform, do you want to become involved in that?’ The answer is immediately yes. Who wouldn’t?

“So the first time I addressed the team, I borrowed a phrase from a Premier League football coach, Fabian Hürzeler from Brighton & Hove Albion, I heard him talking about being ‘brilliant at the basics’.

“That’s what I want our team to do to start with: to be brilliant at the basics. Just make sure the car is reliable, make sure the car is set up properly, let’s get the best from the Bridgestone tyres, let’s be brilliant at the basics. If we do that, we’ll be somewhere near, and then we can build upon that, and I think that’s really what I want our team to do.”

For its GEN4 campaign, Fortescue Zero has opted to run a Jaguar powertrain, giving the Formula E newcomers a strong technical foundation as it prepares to take on one of the most competitive paddocks in the world of motorsport.

GREEN LIGHT FOR GEN4: Inside Fortescue Zero's London Launch

Wright believes the decision was a natural fit for both parties. He said, “Well, Fortescue Zero is a technical partner of Jaguar, so there was absolutely no other choice, really. I think Jaguar TCS Racing are also pleased to have another customer team using their powertrains, because it’s going to be a mighty tough competition in GEN4.

“The value of having three teams operating with the same powertrain is not lost on Jaguar, and it’s certainly not lost on Fortescue. It was a natural fit and a natural choice.”

On the driver front, the team has signed Formula E race winner and fan favourite Dan Ticktum. One of the championship's most established figures, Ticktum brings two career victories to the squad: an impressive maiden triumph at the 2025 Jakarta E-Prix and a memorable last-lap overtake to claim victory in Tokyo in 2026.

Known for his bravado, Ticktum is expected to bring both speed and ambition to the new project. Wright, for one, is confident that the Brit has exactly the qualities the team needs.

He added, “He’s a proven race winner and he’s got fantastic racecraft. You saw him win the Tokyo E-Prix on the very last lap with a really audacious move. He’s fast, he’s fearless, he’s brave and he wants it. He is really, really hungry. To me, there can be no finer attribute than a hungry racing driver.”

Fortescue Zero enters the championship backed by an impressive motorsport heritage. Across its wider motorsport activities, the company boasts an extensive record of 134 pole positions, 378 podiums, 147 victories, nine drivers’ championships and 12 manufacturers’ championships across top-tier racing categories.

Despite those achievements, Wright is reluctant to put a number on what the team should seek to accomplish in its first season. Rather than setting rigid expectations, his focus is on building the strongest possible foundation and allowing the results to follow.

“I don’t think we are setting ourselves any targets. I’m not saying a minimum number of points. I’m not saying we’ve got to win (X) races or whatever. I don’t want to set any limits on what we can achieve.

“I think that in Formula E, when you start with a really strong technical package, which we will be, and fast drivers, then you can be successful, and I want us to be as successful as we possibly can, as quickly as we can. I want to set no limit on how we do that.”

title: What Formula E Teams are Really Doing at Pre-season Testing
excerpt:
Ever wondered what teams are ACTUALLY looking for at pre-season testing? Well, former Formula E Chief Engineer, Albert Lau has got you covered.

When the light turns green at pre-season testing and the cars finally hit the track for the first time, it’s natural to look straight at the timing screens to see who is fastest and make all sorts of presumptions about the season to come.

However, inside the garages, being quickest is rarely the main priority - especially when everyone is learning how to run a brand-new generation of race car!

Formula E Pre-Season Testing: Everything you need to know about GEN4 in Madrid

Back to basics

The minute that you get to pre-season testing you move from a state of operational readiness to race readiness. How do you manage two-car operations with a single PIT BOOST station? How do the engineers run through the various checklists, and how would they run two cars at the same time when you've got one tyre technician, one tyre engineer? Or how do you work with mission control back at home?

That's a really big thing for here - procedural sign-off. So, what happens in a Red Flag? What happens if you have a Safety Car? These are actually things that could happen during a test day here in pre-season testing, and again, it's just making sure you have those things sort of ready to go. And then if some of the things are like, "Okay, this wasn't working well and that was working well," you can still make tweaks before the first race of the season.

The operational excellence is still very important.

The importance of performance

Teams will definitely utilise the benefit of having two cars. You can test these items in a more scientific way because you've got two cars at your disposal. Even though the drivers are different, the fact that they're working from the same base means that you can still compare items across the cars and make sure you have a comprehensive pictures of what's working and what isn't.

There will be a lot of focus here on tyres and then all the control systems. And then for the drivers, it's just mileage, they haven't done enough driving yet with these cars and every circuit they go to is new, so again, that's important. You may start seeing some qualifying simulations as well. We're already doing the race exercises, but teams don't want to show their hand either in terms of strategy, so it'll be a little bit more vanilla. But little things matter.

Maybe at the end of the week on Friday, you may see teams even go to the detail of running the car off-track to pick up rubber to simulate what they would do at the end of the race, just to weigh the tyres to see how much pick up they can grab. It's really detailed stuff that teams will be looking to do and learn from.

What happens to the information gathered at testing?

The engineering teams in Formula E are small enough that it's not like an Formula One where it's a huge scale team. You're still talking about relatively small operational and engineering teams. A lot of them (the engineers) will be listening from home, reading all the reports, and virtually joining the meetings happening at track. In the experienced teams, it should run like clockwork, everybody has a pretty good sense of what they should be doing.

But for some of the new teams, it's a baptism of fire. Some of these mechanics and drivers haven't run a Formula E car before, so this championship in particular is a massively steep learning curve. The cars are super complicated, and without a doubt it's difficult.

Measuring success

Teams obviously come here with a plan for what they want to do, and if you've met your targets for the mileage and you've come close to completing your run plans: in terms of, "right, we came here to test these 10 things and out of those 10 things, we've got a clear read on seven of them" - then happy days, you've achieved what you wanted to do.

It's being clear with your objectives, what you want to do, and being able to achieve them. And if you can do that, it doesn't necessarily mean that you have to be top of the timesheets, it's more like, "right, these are the things we wanted to do, and we achieved them, and we could do it without any issue." That, for me, is a successful test.

title: Formula E Pre-Season Testing: Everything You Need to Know About GEN4 in Madrid
excerpt:
With new drivers, new teams, an updated race format, AND a brand-new generation of all-electric machinery to master, Formula E is back in action for the start of the GEN4 era with pre-season testing in Madrid.

The ABB FIA Formula E World Championship returns with a fresh look as teams and drivers prepare to hit the track for a crucial week of preparation ahead of the 2027 Season. With the debut of the GEN4 car, every garage has more test items than ever to tick off the list.

While headline lap times don't always tell the full story of what's to come in the season ahead, setting the benchmark in Madrid will give drivers and teams a vital boost of confidence before the opening round in Mexico City (16 January).

When and where is testing being held?

The Circuito de Madrid Jarama – RACE will host Formula E pre-season testing from 16 to 20 November 2026 ahead of the 2027 season. After staging last season’s inaugural Madrid E-Prix, the circuit is an ideal venue for teams to hit the track and gather vital early data.

Featuring an undulating layout with a blend of slow and fast corners alongside flat-out straights, Jarama will allow teams to put their new GEN4 machines through their paces across a wide range of conditions - aided by Spain’s mild autumn climate.

Spain has hosted Formula E pre-season testing every year since 2017, with Valencia's Circuit Ricardo Tormo holding the event in all but one of those campaigns. However, this isn't Jarama's first time stepping up for pre-season duties, having previously hosted testing in 2024 after severe flooding in the Valencia region.

There are six sessions due to take place across three days of action during testing week. All times local (UTC+1):

Why do teams go testing?

While teams and drivers rely on advanced simulators, computers, and AI tools to maximise their preparation before hitting the circuit, nothing beats real-world track time.

Digital simulations are only as accurate as the physical data behind them, meaning teams must run on track to validate and refine their models for the season ahead. Crucially, real-world testing also uncovers hidden issues that never appear in a simulator - giving garages vital breathing room to solve problems before the season opener in Mexico City.

Beyond the machinery, testing is about human integration. With new drivers and team principals settling into unfamiliar environments, the entire garage from strategists to mechanics uses the week to build chemistry and rehearse high-pressure procedures in real time.

Ultimately, the primary goal in Madrid isn't topping the timesheets; it's logging as many laps as possible. As a result, testing is often far better at revealing which teams are in trouble than predicting who will be the team to beat!

What exactly will the teams be testing?

With everything new at the start of the GEN4 era, there will be plenty of items to tick off every team’s list. First on the agenda are the new tyres, supplied by Bridgestone for the first time in Formula E history. Teams will need to figure out their durability, how to prepare them for qualifying laps, and how hard drivers can push on them across varying conditions.

Alongside the new rubber, there are two race formats this season – E-Prix and E-PrixUnleashed. Teams must learn how the cars operate across different conditions and race lengths, as well as with the high and low-downforce settings available over a race weekend.

EXPLAINED: Formula E's new sporting format for the 2027 Season

Teams will also need to get to grips with their new powertrains and the 600 kW of power available in ATTACK MODE as part of the GEN4 package, including how energy recharges and the best way to manage it over an E-Prix distance with PIT BOOST.

At Fusion DTM Champion Ayhancan Güven kickstarts the 2027 campaign for the all-electric newcomers and at Fortescue Zero Racing Paul Aron takes the wheel.

While all six rookies boast strong track records in open-wheel racing, none have started a Formula E race, and their prior experience in rookie tests and free practice sessions vary. For each of them, the immediate priority in Madrid will be settling into their new environments while adapting to a different style of racing and brand-new all-electric machinery.

However, with every team starting fresh on the new cars this year, the learning curve should be less of a disadvantage as the rookies look to make an immediate impression in their maiden Formula E campaigns.

title: Fusion enters the 2027 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship
excerpt:
British-based Fusion will enter the championship ahead of the 2027 season, the first of the GEN4 era with two state-of-the-art Porsche 975 RSE race cars.

Joining the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship as a Porsche customer team, the all-new squad will be led by Formula E veteran, Phil Charles. After a successful career in Formula One, Charles joined Jaguar TCS Racing in 2017, first as Technical Director and then as Deputy Team Principal, earning multiple accolades along the way.

“There's something special about building a racing team from the ground up," said Fusion's new Team Principal Phil Charles. "You have the opportunity to bring together people you believe in, establish the right culture and create an environment where everyone can perform at their best."

“We know exactly how competitive Formula E is, and we're under no illusions about the challenge ahead. But we've assembled a fantastic group of people, we have a strong technical partner in Porsche, and everyone is working incredibly hard to get us ready. We're not here simply to make up the numbers. We want to build a team that can compete at the front, and that's what we're working towards.”

For investment group Fusion, today's announcement follows the recent launch of junior single-seater operation 'LN4 Fusion' which will see the brand enter the FIA Formula 2 Championship next year, in partnership with 2025 Formula One World Champion, Lando Norris.

NORRIS: "The level of drivers you have here is top - it's as good as you get."

“Building the right team has been our priority from day one," says Dan Richards, CEO of Fusion Racing. "In Phil Charles and Chris Bluett, we have two highly experienced people who understand what it takes to compete at this level, and we've been fortunate to attract some exceptional talent to join them.

“I'm incredibly proud of the team we're putting together. There's a huge amount of work ahead, but I couldn't have more confidence in the people leading that effort.”

Fusion joins the Formula E paddock at the start of an exciting new chapter for the world's leading all-electric championship. Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

The team will announce their full driver line-up in due course.

title: Mahindra Racing introduces the M13Electro as GEN4 era begins
excerpt:
Mahindra Racing have unveiled the M13Electro, its challenger for the 2027 Season of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

With Formula E's pre-season testing in Madrid due to begin in less than 24 hours, Mahindra Racing have revealed their brand new challenger for the 2027 Season - the first of the GEN4 era.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

The M13Electro was unveiled through a dedicated digital launch campaign, giving fans around the world their first look at Mahindra Racing's challenger for the GEN4 era. Featuring the team's signature red, a defining colour of Mahindra Racing's identity, the new livery celebrates the team's heritage while looking ahead to a new generation of electric motorsport.

Taking the wheel of the M13Electro will be the experienced partnership of Edoardo Mortara and Nyck de Vries, who enter their fourth season as teammates. Both drivers have played a crucial role in the development of the team's GEN4 machinery, through close collaboration with the Banbury-based squad's engineers.

Last season, Mahindra delivered one of their strongest campaigns in Formula E history, finishing 3rd in the Teams' Championship with 252 points - a significant jump from 4th place (186 points) the prior year. Both drivers remained firmly in title contention until the final round of the season in London - securing their positions at the team for the start of the GEN4 era.

Nyck de Vries, Mahindra Racing Driver, said: “GEN4 represents a significant step forward for Formula E, and it's exciting to be part of that transition. The changes to the car are substantial, particularly in terms of power, four-wheel drive and overall performance, so there will be a lot for us as drivers to understand and adapt to.

"Developing a completely new generation of car is always a complex process, and the collaboration between the drivers and engineering team will be crucial in understanding where we can find performance."

Edoardo Mortara, Mahindra Racing Driver, said: “The arrival of GEN4 is a very important moment for Formula E, as the new regulations bring a completely different level of performance and some interesting technical challenges.

"From a driver's perspective, understanding how to get the maximum out of the new package will be a key part of the process. There is a lot of work involved in building a competitive car, and our experience from the previous seasons will be important in helping the team make the right steps throughout development."

title: Who’s On the Grid? Formula E’s 2027 Driver Line-up So Far
excerpt:
Ahead of the 2027 Season – and the start of Formula E's GEN4 era – here are the drivers confirmed to be racing on the grid.

Ahead of Pre-Season Testing in Jarama, Madrid, next week, these are the drivers that have secured race seats for the 2027 Formula E Season – the first of the all-new and exciting GEN4 era.

From respected rookies, big driver changes and the return of lots of familiar faces, these are all the drivers that will be taking to the track for the first-taste of GEN4 across the 2027 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship season when the season starts on 16 January in Mexico City.

Who are the new drivers this season?

Currently, there are four new names with full-time Formula E seats for next season. First to be announced is French driver Théo Pourchaire with the Opel GSE Formula E Team. Known as one of racing’s brightest talents, Pourchaire works as a Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team Development Driver and is a former Formula 2 World Champion.

Elsewhere, Paysafe Envision Racing announced Zak O'Sullivan would be promoted to a full-time seat, after the Brit has been the team’s Simulator Driver and participated in several Rookie Tests for them over the GEN3 era. O'Sullivan has also been busy in Super Formula this year, and won the prestigious Autosport BRDC Award in 2021.

Over at Lola Formula E Team, it's an all-rookie affair with Robert Shwartzman and Enzo Fittipaldi both set to make their Formula E debuts. 25-year-old Brazilian Fittipaldi joins the all-electric championship, having previously taken part in the 2024 Berlin Rookie Test, whilst former FIA Formula 3 champion Shwartzman brings extensive experience across single-seater and endurance racing to the Lola squad.

A new era of the all-electric championship resulted in quite the driver market reshuffle, with lots of drivers changing teams during our off-season. Dan Ticktum has relocated to the new Fortescue Zero Racing team, Zane Maloney has moved to Nissan and Mitch Evans departed Jaguar TCS Racing after a decade to switch things up with the new Opel entry. title: How Stoffel Vandoorne is bouncing back in GEN4 with Jaguar
excerpt:
The 2021/22 Formula E World Champion is back in Formula E for a new generation of car, racing with Jaguar TCS Racing.

Stoffel Vandoorne – a former FIA Formula E World Champion – will be back on the grid full-time next season, becoming a Jaguar TCS Racing driver alongside teammate António Félix da Costa. For the Belgian driver, who had four wins, 17 podiums and 103 career race starts to his name, this move up from a sabbatical as the team’s Reserve and Development driver has come at the perfect time.

Having had a year out of the World Championship, after the departure of Maserati MSG Racing into the Citroën Racing outfit, Stoffel Vandoorne hasn’t just been sitting on the sidelines. The former Formula 1 driver has been actively testing the GEN4 Jaguar machines all year, ahead of Pre-Season Testing across 16-20 November next week.

“I am still the same driver,” Vandoorne begins, “I am still very talented and motivated and I think success in motorsport has its ups and downs and I don't think anyone has been on top all the time in their career - everyone has had to deal a little bit with setbacks.

“For sure in some parts of GEN3 weren’t my best form, but I am also learning and carrying that experience forward and how to reset and learn about a completely new car.

Vandoorne started his Formula E career with HWA, just three weeks after leaving Formula 1. Just five races into his rookie season, he had placed his car on pole position for the 2019 Hong Kong E-Prix and very quickly cemented himself as one of the championship’s brightest emerging talents.

A season later he was representing both Mercedes-Benz EQ in Formula E as a full-time driver, whilst also working as a Reserve Driver in F1. He, and then-teammate Nyck de Vries, would then win back-to-back drivers’ honours, with Vandoorne taking the drivers’ title in 2021.

After their leave from the all-electric championship, Vandoorne made the move to DS PENSKE for two seasons before joining the Maserati squad. After a year on the sidelines at Jaguar as a third driver last season, Vandoorne is now back racing full-time in the series and has a new machine to get behind the wheel of.

“GEN4 is going to be very different, and a lot more powerful and technical in some aspects as well,” Vandoorne continued. “I have also got a great [Jaguar] team around me, and with a team that has been one of the dominant teams in GEN3. They have won two Constructors' World Championships, so they have been top class of their field and when I joined them last year it was a great experience to see how exactly they were different to some of my previous teams that I have been with.

READ MORE: GEN4 - a new benchmark for speed, sustainability and innovation in motorsport

“I have a huge belief in those guys that they're going to be competitive again in GEN4 and I am very happy to be a part of that.”

As well as testing the GEN4, Vandoorne has been competing in the World Endurance Championship with Peugeot and continuing his Test and Reserve Driver duties with Aston Martin in F1, adding “it doesn’t feel that long” since he’s been away.

He fills the seat of Mitch Evans, who parted ways with the Jaguar brand after 10 years for a new challenge at Opel.

“I don't think that adds anything extra,” he added, when talking about the pressure of replacing the series’ most successful driver in terms of wins – with 16 to his name, all with Jaguar. “I think we are all very talented racing drivers and the nature of racing is people move around – especially in a competitive championship – so you are always kind of stepping into someone's shoes or seat with high expectations.

“I think any of the top teams that you are racing for, you are always expected to perform and that pressure ultimately comes from myself, because I want to perform at my highest level myself so I don’t see anything different to be honest. It's kind of a mutual pressure we want to perform and live up to the past performances and to make sure we carry that momentum from last year into next year.”

The signing of Vandoorne and Da Costa is one of just a few line-ups in the championship’s history where both drivers have won championship titles. However, this is familiar territory for both racers, with Da Costa previously pairing up with Pascal Wehrlein at Porsche and Vandoorne teammates with Jean-Eric Vergne at DS PENSKE.

“I don’t see any issues at all,” the new Jaguar signing commented, when asked about inner-team competition between the two. “I have known Antonio for a very long time, he has been a champion as well in the past, same as me.

“It depends a lot on how both personalities embrace that, and how the team handles it as well, so I think it’s a combination of both how that relationship ends up working. We have been very hard competitors for most of our junior careers and then into Formula E. Obviously there is always competitiveness between us, but ultimately we are racing for one of the biggest teams in Formula E. We have to respect the team, and we are always going to be professional in that way as well.

“Especially in this initial phase of GEN4, it's all a little bit unknown, and we don't really know how competitive we are going to be. We are working extremely closely together and we are pushing the team as much as we can and there are not really any games being played or any hiding. It is really ‘let’s make our car as competitive as we can and hopefully we are strong enough to fight it out on track between us’.”

title: Formula E announce 2027 calendar update for Jeddah and Sanya E-Prix

title: Green light for GEN4: Inside Fortescue Zero’s London Launch

This is far from Fortescue’s first foray into motorsport, from its roots in Williams Racing (as Williams Advanced Engineering), to becoming an in-demand, high-performance engineering business, working at the cutting edge of electrification as the Official PIT BOOST supplier of Formula E.

"We have an amazing Chairman, who loves competing," said Pichot. "He took a very easy task to compete against the fossil fuel industry. The only way we're going to do this is by being on the front foot of innovation...we're going to decarbonise our operations.

"It's an amazing challenge, but there was something missing. How do we keep on the front foot of technology? Formula E, batteries, electrification, a better world for all of us and for our kids."

Ticktum's new chapter

Dan Ticktum also seized his moment in the spotlight during his maiden appearance with his new outfit. The 27-year-old Brit looked right at home, reflecting on his decision to commit to Fortescue over rival offers for the GEN4 era.

"Formula E was founded 12 years ago," Dodds recalled. "And it wasn't founded only as a racing series... we wanted to be a World Championship racing series to create incredibly fast racing cars, but we had two other missions at the same time. One was to be a platform for sustainability... and the other was to create a laboratory on the race track to advance the energy transition.

"They're (Fortescue) not on this journey to be just racing World Champions. They want to be environmental champions. They want to be champions for the earth, for the planet, for the next generation."

The GEN4 Formula E car is a radical reimagining of electric racing, featuring an even more aggressive 5,540mm x 1,800mm footprint designed to harness a massive 600kW (815bhp) output. This futuristic chassis introduces two aerodynamic packages that switch between high-downforce qualifying and low-drag race modes to exceed 200 mph, and permanent All-Wheel Drive for unprecedented traction.

GEN4 promises to deliver the fastest-ever lap time seen by a Formula E car - at least five seconds per lap faster on street circuits - compared to the most recent generation, the GEN3 Evo.

The covers come off

The launch concluded with the official reveal of Fortescue Zero's all-new challenger for the 2027 season. Retaining the team's distinctive neon green visual identity with a refined, aerodynamic finish, the car showcases the next evolution of Fortescue’s motorsport presence.

At the core of the operation is the squad's new technical partnership, with the entry powered by a Jaguar GEN4 powertrain. Combining Jaguar’s championship winning engineering pedigree with the raw speed and race winning capabilities of Ticktum, Fortescue Zero has seemingly assembled the ingredients necessary to mount an impressive debut campaign.

title: "I’ll prove the doubters wrong": Dan Ticktum on finding a home with Fortescue Zero Racing for GEN4

At the start of a brand new chapter with Fortescue Zero Racing, can the paddock’s most candid driver turn doubters into believers?

Dan Ticktum has always been one of the most entertaining and honest drivers in the Formula E paddock - qualities which have made him an undeniable fan favourite. But at the end of last season, a huge question mark hung over his future in the all-electric championship, with the London-born driver uncertain about whether he would secure a spot on the grid for the start of the GEN4 era.

However, the Dan Ticktum that walked on stage at the Shoreditch Electric venue on Friday was confident and excited about the start of a new chapter, after finding a home with Formula E newcomers, Fortescue Zero Racing.

"There was a time a couple of months ago where I thought I might not have a seat full stop," reiterated Dan. "I then quite quickly got a few offers and this was always at the top of the pile.

I feel like I can do the driving round in circles pretty much better than anyone. But you know, sometimes people can be a bit skeptical about how I can represent a brand. So I feel like I will prove all the doubters wrong."

The team itself will likely have its doubters, with the whole operation coming together in just two months, following Fortescue Zero's successful acquisition of the PENSKE operation. Yet, despite the quick turnaround, Ticktum has total confidence in the new venture.

"I've only been with the team for a few weeks," he says. "And I've tried to get in the simulator as much as possible and understand the Jaguar systems and try and get to grips with things.

"I think there's very good people and the right level of investment to win races consistently. So, for me as a driver, it's very motivating. They're a great bunch of guys."

Fortescue Zero are no strangers to motorsport, from its roots in Williams Racing (as Williams Advanced Engineering), to becoming an in-demand, high-performance engineering business, working at the cutting edge of electrification as the Official PIT BOOST supplier of Formula E.

Their entrance to the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship coincides with the all-new GEN4 era, a radical reimagining of electric racing, featuring an even more aggressive 5,540mm x 1,800mm footprint designed to harness a massive 600kW (815bhp) output. title: Formula E's dramatic history in the USA
excerpt:
From title deciders to home heroes and intense fights for the win, here’s a look back at Formula E’s best moments in the United States

The ABB FIA Formula E World Championship has featured at least one round in the United States in all but one of its 12 seasons to date. In 2027, The Circuit of the Americas (COTA) in Austin, Texas, becomes the seventh US venue to host the all-electric championship.

Over the years, the undulating road circuit has hosted America’s premier racing categories - IndyCar, NASCAR, and IMSA. It has also welcomed Formula 1, MotoGP, and WEC, with Formula E now becoming the latest world championship to race around the Austin venue.

From downtown street tracks and waterfront views to iconic permanent road courses, here is the story of Formula E across the United States.

Venue

Season(s)

Biscayne Bay (Miami)

S1 (2015)

Long Beach Street Circuit

S1 & S2 (2015 & 2016)

Brooklyn Street Circuit (New York)

S3-S5, S7 & S8 (2017-2019 & 2021-22)

Portland International Raceway

S9 & S10 (2023 & 2024)

Homestead-Miami Speedway

S11 (2025)

Miami International Autodrome

S12 & Season 2027 (2026 & 2027)

Circuit of the Americas (Austin)

Season 2027

Home hero’s near miss in Miami

For the inaugural Formula E season, two races were held in America. The first of these was in downtown Miami at Biscayne Bay in what turned out to be the venue's only race.

The 1.3-mile temporary street circuit wound around the home of the NBA team Miami Heat and provided great racing in its sole appearance.

Jean-Éric Vergne secured pole position by 0.05 of a second and battled with Sam Bird early in the race, but both hit issues during the E-Prix. This left Nico Prost and Daniel Abt to battle for the lead, but Abt hit power problems of his own. Prost then battled debutant and home hero Scott Speed, keeping his calm to win in the all-electric championship for the first time.

History repeats itself at Long Beach

Just weeks after the inaugural stateside race, Formula E swapped the East Coast for the West Coast for its first race at Long Beach in California, one of the USA’s most historic street courses.

Prost and Abt continued where they left off in Miami, securing the front row, but it was Nelson Piquet Jr. who sprinted off into the lead at the start. The Brazilian held off Vergne, Lucas di Grassi and Sebastien Buemi to win his first Formula E race, 35 years after his father took his maiden Formula One win at the same venue.

The following year, di Grassi overcame a disqualification in the previous race in Mexico and secured a crucial win at Long Beach, taking the lead in the Drivers’ Championship by a single point over Buemi.

READ MORE: "A sense of duty done": Lucas di Grassi's final Formula E chapter

Taking it to the Big Apple

Formula E raced in New York City with a double-header event every year between 2017 and 2022, aside from the COVID-19-affected 2020 season, with the technical Brooklyn Street Circuit looking over the spectacular Manhattan and Jersey City skyline.

Twice hosting the season finale, New York often produced dramatic races with championship defining results. For the very first race, debutant Alex Lynn stunned the field by securing pole position, before retiring in the race, with Sam Bird taking victory.

Debutants continued to take centre stage in the second race of the weekend, with future F1 race winner Pierre Gasly finishing the race in fourth. Despite crashing on the last corner, the Frenchman was able to hold position and scramble across the finish line. At the same time, di Grassi picked up important points in his title fight against the absent Buemi, while Bird made it back-to-back victories.

READ MORE: Formula 1 drivers that also raced in Formula E

New York holds very good memories for Vergne, who clinched both of his Formula E titles in Brooklyn. As GEN1 wound down, Vergne took the championship on Bastille Day, despite being excluded from qualifying. He charged through the field to fifth to clinch the title, and rounded out the era with a win a day later.

A year later, at the start of the GEN2 era, Vergne defended his crown despite a turbulent double-header. A late-race collision with Felipe Massa in Race 1 pushed the title fight to the finale, where a seventh-place finish was enough to seal the championship.

The first race of the 2022 double-header in the Big Apple will forever be remembered for the sudden deluge which hit the circuit, sending several drivers into the barrier and forcing a Red Flag to end the race early. Despite his car being wedged in the barriers, Nick Cassidy secured his first Formula E win.

Da Costa brought Formula E’s New York chapter to an unforgettable close. Starting from pole, the DS Techeetah driver delivered a commanding lights-to-flag victory, holding off a charging Stoffel Vandoorne before famously celebrating with a dive into the Hudson River. While da Costa took the spoils, runner-up Vandoorne seized the championship lead - a crucial step toward clinching his maiden Drivers' Championship in Seoul just a few weeks later.

Tense battles at Portland

As the GEN3 era dawned, the series relocated stateside to Portland International Raceway for the next two seasons. The wide, flowing Oregon road course transformed races into tactical high-speed chess matches, defined by dramatic slipstreaming and intense energy conservation.

Portland’s debut, which featured numerous overtakes, was won by Nick Cassidy from 10th on the grid ahead of polesitter Jake Dennis, in a race which proved pivotal to the Englishman’s championship hopes.

Portland expanded to a double-header the following year, and da Costa dominated the weekend with back-to-back victories over Robin Frijns. Marking four wins in five races, the clean sweep reignited his season and kept his outside title hopes alive.

Return to the Sunshine State

Miami returned to the Formula E calendar for the 2024/25 season with the enhanced GEN3 Evo. The Homestead-Miami Speedway, host of the NASCAR Cup finale for many years, including in 2026, held a Formula E race for the only time that year.

Norman Nato was on course to secure victory in the race which was halted due to a Red Flag, but he was one of several drivers who failed to use all the ATTACK MODE allocation before the end of the race. This handed victory to Pascal Wehrlein in a race which totally opened up the title race.

The Miami International Autodrome joined the calendar for the following season. - the home of the Miami Dolphins marked the third destination in Florida for Formula E.

Conditions were treacherous for the circuit’s debut as rain fell ahead of the start. After securing his first pole, Nico Müller was denied a maiden victory by an inspired Mitch Evans, climbing from ninth on the grid around the 1.4-mile circuit to pass Müller with a crucial switchback overtake.

The Miami Gardens venue also hosted the inaugural Formula E EVO Sessions in 2025, with well-known celebrities such as Sergio Aguero and Tom Felton, and creators such as Driver61 and JUCA, taking to the track to test out the all-electric GEN3 machinery.

New chapter in the Lone Star State

The calendar expands to Texas next season as COTA plays host to the dawn of the GEN4 era.

The maiden Austin E-Prix serves as the opening act of an American double-bill, with the Miami E-Prix following just two weeks later - bringing Formula E's cutting-edge electric performance to one of North America’s premier racing venues.

From street circuits to world-class road courses, the stateside rounds of the all-electric championship have always delivered high drama, and Austin promises to raise the stakes even higher.

title: Nissan's Maloney targets Formula E glory and a trackside visit from Rihanna
excerpt:
Barbadian driver Zane Maloney is stepping up to his biggest Formula E season yet with Nissan, and opened up about his family's racing roots, his idol Lewis Hamilton, and his goal to invite Rihanna to a race.

Known as ‘the boy from Barbados’, Zane Maloney is preparing for his biggest season of Formula E yet. The 23-year old will be representing Nissan for the first season of GEN4, and racing alongside World Champion teammate Oliver Rowland in 2026/27.

Having raced and won in several junior categories, and becoming the first Barbadian driver to win a race in FIA Formula 3 and FIA Formula 2, Zane Maloney also earned Reserve Driver roles for Red Bull Racing and Sauber in Formula 1.

In an interview conducted earlier this season, Maloney opened up about his family passion for racing, as well as his racing hero Lewis Hamilton and trying to get Rihanna to a Formula E race.

“There's a lot of motorsports in Barbados,” Maloney explained. “So my entire family – so my grandad, my two uncles, my dad, two of my older cousins – were drivers or they are drivers. So from when I was one to two years old, I was at the racetrack every weekend, and I was three when I first drove.

“I used to do like six or seven different sports at school, but racing was always my passion. I guess because of my family, it was all of our passion, so I started then. It was for fun, of course, in Barbados and we didn't even think of anything more than that. Then it started to become a bit more serious, and I got the sponsors I needed from back home, and I just kept going up the rankings each year and I never did more than one year in a category.”

A love for Lewis Hamilton

As to be expected, racing drivers also have their own racing heroes. The same goes for Maloney, who has always been a proud supporter of seven-time World Champion Lewis Hamilton. The Scuderia Ferrari driver has certainly inspired several drivers across international motorsport, with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar also sharing his admiration for the F1 legend in recent years.

“I was four years old when Lewis went into F1, so it was Lewis from the beginning,” Maloney confessed when asked about Hamilton. “He came to Barbados in 2014 and drove go-karts with us and I kind of always looked up to him in the sense of on-track, and then every time I met him in those early stages he was very nice and down to earth, so off-track as well.”

Maloney has also said in the past that he picked racing number 22 as a tribute to Hamilton. “[Hamilton] is 44, and I was like if I can be half as good as him then 22.” Makes sense!

Being from Barbados is clearly something Maloney takes great pride with, as the Caribbean country only has a population of 280,000. It has been the birthplace of several sports stars, such as cricketers and NFL players, but there haven’t been any triumphant racing driver exports aside from Zane.

“Like I said, everyone in Barbados loves motorsports, but no one's ever taken it to a professional level or overseas. So, when I started travelling, everyone kind of came behind me and supported me, but all the races were at 3am their time! I got a lot of support, of course, grateful for it, and also trying to make it as far as possible in my career, do as well as possible, so that young kids coming up can see that and also dream to be a professional driver.”

Receiving support from Rihanna

But perhaps, the best known person from the country is global pop phenomenon Rihanna, who is one of Maloney’s close supporters. After winning both rounds in FIA Formula 2 across the first race weekend in Bahrain a few years ago, Maloney received a special message and a follow on Instagram from the singer-songwriter and businesswoman.

“Obviously Rihanna is from Barbados,” Maloney begins, as he explains how the connection between the two began. “She's done amazing things, and I think it was in Bahrain in 2024 when I won both races in the same weekend that I got a message. She followed me and I got a message from her and I thought it was a fan account.

“Since then, she's been supporting me. There were talks, and she wanted to come to Miami last year, but she had other things to do at the last minute, so she couldn't come. So I'm trying. We're trying to get her to a race!

“I'm sure she would love it, but also, and she's given a lot of support. So yeah, grateful for that. It's cool to see celebrities or stars or people doing well in their different genres being from Barbados.”

Looking ahead to GEN4 with Nissan

Back in the present, Maloney has been speaking to Nissan’s media team about how he’s been finding the new team and a brand-new machine to understand.

“The GEN4 car is a big step up,” Maloney confirmed. “With the active differential, permanent all-wheel drive, 600kW of power and more downforce than before, it’s really enjoyable to drive. It’s an exciting moment for the series and we’re confident it will take Formula E to the next level. Nobody quite knows what to expect, but my first laps in the GEN4 car were great.

“In the first race, everyone will be learning so that makes it extra important to be on the pace quickly and start the season with good results.

“I think as a driver, you’re always changing your style, even from race-to-race in the same car. One of the most important skills to have is to be adaptable to the car, circuit and conditions on any particular day. We’re already focused on what we can try in testing to know what tools we have at our disposal for when the time comes to go racing.

NEWS: Nissan confirm Bird and Pulling at Formula E Team into GEN4

“We’re going to a lot of great circuits next season, including some I have good memories of. I won my British F4 title at Brands Hatch and I took victory at Zandvoort in Formula 3, two tracks I really enjoy. COTA looks like an incredible circuit, with a fast and flowing Sector 1. Generally, we go to some really cool tracks in Formula E so I’m looking forward to it all.”

Maloney and teammate Oliver Rowland will be at Pre-Season Testing at Circuito del Jarama, Spain on 16-20 November.

title: The Heartbeat of Motorsport: Celebrating FIA Volunteers and Officials Month
excerpt:
During FIA Volunteers and Officials Month, volunteers and officials from across the globe shared what drives them to selflessly give their time to racing events.

When the lights go out and race cars leave the grid, all eyes turn to the high-speed action on track. But behind every Formula E race weekend lies an extraordinary, dedicated workforce working tirelessly behind the scenes.

As part of FIA Volunteers and Officials Month, the FIA and the wider motorsport community is shining a spotlight on the unsung heroes whose passion, dedication, and fast-thinking keep our drivers, fans and teams safe, and our E-Prix's running smoothly.

Without these dedicated individuals, who often go unnoticed, race weekends simply could not happen. From trackside "orange marshals" managing safety during live sessions, to officials overseeing event logistics, volunteers give up their time purely for the love of the sport. Volunteering in motorsport also builds a global family - a welcoming community where people from all backgrounds and corners of the world unite over a shared love for racing.

Technical excellence

Beyond the trackside action, technical precision forms a core pillar of the volunteer operation. FIA technical delegates and scrutineers work around the clock to ensure every car strictly adheres to technical and sporting regulations. Post-session checks on the weighbridge measure everything from overall weight and weight distribution to car dimensions and tire pressures.

During active sessions, scrutineers monitor over 1,400 data points per car, analysing more real-time parameters than individual teams can process to guarantee fairness across the grid. Many technical volunteers bring real-world experience from mechanics and engineering, often starting their journey through simple "marshal taster days" at tracks like Donington Park before branching out and volunteering at a wide range of global motorsport events.

The human connection

"I know I have a family no matter where I go, not only here in the United States," says Danya, a motorsport volunteer from Guatemala. "I know I can always find a community and find my people that love racing." It's this mutual love and desire to be close to the sport that is echoed time and time again by the volunteers who show up come rain or shine, but for others the connection goes even deeper.

For some, the inspiration and drive to be involved in volunteering is deeply personal and rooted in family legacy. Erin, a volunteer from Texas, followed directly in her father’s footsteps to step into the circuit.

EXPLAINED: Formula E's new sporting format for the 2026/27 season

"What inspired me to become a volunteer in motorsport is actually my Dad," she shares. "He has done this for quite a while and it really interested me when I was younger. So, when I got the ability to come help out where I could, I took it."

For FIA Volunteers and Officials Month, Formula E wants to thank every volunteer who selflessly gives their time to keep Formula E events safe for everyone.

title: Opel Team Principal Schrott hints to “very solid reliability” with GEN4 so far
excerpt:
Opel GSE Formula E Team Principal Jörg Schrott opens up about the processes behind their new Formula E outfit, how testing has been ahead of the first GEN4 season and the excellent reaction to their striking new livery choice.

Jörg Schrott is no stranger to Opel, having started work at the German automobile manufacturer in 1997. Since joining, he was notably involved in setting up the brand’s former motorsport arm and has been head of Opel Motorsport since 2012.

Now Team Principal to their new Formula E team, Schrott detailed the timeline of Opel’s entry into all-electric single-seaters whilst at this month’s Paris Motor Show.

Opel’s GEN4 timeline explained

“We started the GEN4 programme over two years ago, and the programme progressed through all the development areas in the meantime,” Opel’s Team Principal Schrott began. “Starting with the design of the vehicle, of the components, all the work on the test benches, on the dino, on the simulation, the incorporation of the systems into the car, and then we started the test sessions on track. First proving the reliability, the validation of the package, and then, finally, the optimisation of the performance.

“Now, the whole programme is shifting, increasingly to prepare the whole package for race operation.

“We have a few milestones to pass by in the upcoming weeks, so we have the FIA homologation and we have to build up the cars. We have to do the shakedown of the cars, and then very important is the final test sessions in Spain, especially the full [official pre-season] testing in Jarama. This is very important to us, not only, you know, to check and to optimise the little things on the car, but also the whole team has to demonstrate the performance in terms of race operations under real race conditions.

“The goal is pretty clear. We have to arrive in Jarama with two fully prepared cars and with a team which is able to deliver in terms of race organisation, in terms of race operation on a very high performance level from the very beginning.”

How testing has been for Evans and Pourchaire

Opel have signed one of the most talked about line-ups on the current grid, with Mitch Evans and Théo Pourchaire confirmed for 2026/27. For Evans, it’s a huge move as he leaves Jaguar TCS Racing after a decade together – and as the driver with the most wins in Formula E’s history – for a new venture, whereas Pourchaire will be a rookie but comes with heaps of experience as the 2023 FIA Formula 2 Champion.

NEWS: 10 Biggest Formula E Driver Transfers in Formula E History

“To date we completed 12 test days and were running approximately 6,000 kilometres and that is a good number, by the way, because our package demonstrated very solid reliability from the very beginning.

“Mitch and Théo played a very important role in our test and development programme, not only the work in the simulator, but also in the real car in the test session. I really can say that the guys, you can feel that they would like to push the whole project forward.

“They are very focussed in terms of feedback to the engineers, and have a very close full collaboration with the whole team. So I can say that they both have arrived in the Opel team, in the Opel family, and of course they are looking forward now to driving their own race car for the very first time, which is a special moment for the drivers.”

It’s been a big few years for the team, who proudly showed off their Opel GSE 27FE machine at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, with Evans, Pourchaire and Test and Development Driver Sophia Flörsch all present.

FIRST LOOK: Opel steps into Formula E's GEN4 era with the GSE 27FE

“It is an awesome [livery] design, I like it and I guess this design brings everything together. Three strong and bold colours – black silver and yellow – pay homage to Opel’s motorsport history, but the design also represents our brand in a fresh and bold way. It also shows the dynamism of racing, and it highlights also the pure performance of our GEN4 race car, so I can say our designers did a fantastic job.”

The livery certainly received a lot of positive feedback from fans, who loved the bright and bold livery that will be seen across the 2026/27 Formula E World Championship campaign.

“The reactions have been very positive since the official announcement that we will enter Formula E,” Schrott concluded, when asked about the general reaction from Opel staff to their new motorsport challenge. “You can feel and see this as the people – regardless of who we are talking about, so the people in the headquarters or in the markets or in the plants, or even our fan community – are really happy and proud that Opal is coming back to the big stage in motorsport.”

title: Callum Voisin Joins Andretti Formula E as Official Development Driver
excerpt:
After representing the American Andretti team at the 2026 Official Rookie Test, Callum Voisin joins the team in a new role.

Andretti Formula E Team have announced the signing of junior talent Callum Voisin, who will be joining the team as its Official Development Driver ahead of the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship season.

Voisin has tested Formula E machinery before, with his first experience of Formula E machinery coming at the 2025 Official Rookie Test in Berlin with CUPRA KIRO where he finished fifth, before joining the American Andretti team for the 2026 Official Rookie Test at Circuito del Jarama in Madrid in March.

The British-Swiss driver will become a key part of the team’s simulator program and race preparation, supporting Jake Dennis, Felipe Drugovich and the engineering team as the series enters its GEN4 era.

Voisin’s racing career to date

20-year-old Callum Voisin joins Andretti after a standout season in Porsche Carrera Cup GB, where he secured the 2026 title with Rosland Gold by Century Motorsport with two races to spare, ending his campaign with nine victories.

That success adds to a racing background spanning single-seaters, sports cars and endurance competition. Having won the 2023 GB3 Championship with Rodin Carlin, Voisin progressed to FIA Formula 3, where he claimed a Feature Race victory from pole position at Spa-Francorchamps in 2024. More recently, he has combined his British Porsche campaign with appearances in Porsche Carrera Cup Italia and competed in the Asian Le Mans Series with High Class Racing.

“I’m really pleased to be joining Andretti Formula E as Official Development Driver,” Voisin said. “Working with the team at the rookie test gave me a great introduction to how everyone operates, so it’s exciting to be building on that relationship. There’s a lot to learn with GEN4 and I’m looking forward to supporting the team to prepare for each race.”

Newly-announced Team Principal Campbell Hobson – who takes over from long-time leader Roger Griffths – sees the position as an opportunity to strengthen the team’s preparation while supporting Voisin’s continued development.

NEWS: Andretti Formula E names Campbell Hobson as new Team Principal

“We’re pleased to welcome Callum into a more permanent role with Andretti Formula E,” Hobson stated. “His work in the simulator will be an important part of our race preparation, supporting our engineers and both drivers as we build our understanding of GEN4. Having already worked together at the rookie test earlier this year, there’s a foundation to build on and his success across different categories demonstrates his ability to adapt to new challenges.”

title: Nissan confirm Bird and Pulling at Formula E Team into GEN4
excerpt:
The 12-time Formula E race winner and F1 Academy Champion remain a key part of Nissan's Formula E operations.

Nissan have confirmed that they will be retaining multiple Formula E race winner Sam Bird, and F1 Academy Champion Abbi Pulling, as part of their 2026/27 campaign in the all-electric championship.

Alongside their announced full-time Formula E drivers, 2024/25 World Champion Oliver Rowland and new signing Zane Maloney, Bird and Pulling will provide essential help for the team both on-site and through simulation work.

Bird continues as Nissan Reserve

Bird joined the Nissan Formula E team in November 2025 and is their Reserve and Development Driver. Having raced in the championship since its inception until the 2024/25 season concluded, Bird achieved 12 wins in that time and won at least one race a year across his first seven seasons – something that has never been achieved since. He is also part of a small group of drivers to have won races across all three generations of cars used in the series.

"Since joining the team I've really enjoyed my time here and been welcomed with open arms,” Bird stated. “We've completed plenty of positive work in the simulator and during testing as we prepare for the GEN4 era.

“With a new car for Season 13, we've spent a lot of time setting the simulator up to ensure we can give Oliver and Zane the most accurate representation of the new features. As the weeks go by, we're developing a stronger understanding of the GEN4 machine and I'm pleased to be contributing to that. My aim for the upcoming season is to continue helping the team to the best of my ability, working with the engineering and strategy sides as well as the drivers so we can maximise our performance."

Pulling remains Rookie and Simulator driver

For Pulling, this news marks another year as the team’s Rookie and Simulator driver. The GB3 race winner – the first woman to accomplish such an achievement – has participated in the Women’s Test with Nissan, as well as Miami Free Practices and the Madrid Rookie Test and is a respected and familiar face within the Formula E paddock.

"I've really enjoyed being with Nissan Formula E Team and I'm delighted to continue in my role as we move into the GEN4 era,” Pulling added. “I've loved my work in the simulator and of course the sessions out on track, which have been the highlight of my time with the team.

“I'm looking forward to exploring what the GEN4 car has to offer, starting in the simulator and then hopefully on race weekends. The new car will be a challenge for everyone, but it looks very exciting and appealing to drivers. A big thank you to the team for the support they've given me so far, and I can't wait to continue into Season 13!"

Bird and Pulling will continue working alongside Rowland and Maloney ahead of Pre-Season Testing at Circuito del Jarama, Spain on 16-20 November.

title: 10 Biggest Formula E Driver Transfers in Formula E History
excerpt:
From championship-winning transfers to shocking grid reshuffles, explore the moves that reshaped the sport.

With Mitch Evans making the bombshell move to Opel GSE Formula E Team this season, having started his Formula E career at Jaguar TCS Racing a decade ago, these are 10 of the biggest driver market swaps that have been seen in the championship since its inception.

From prominent promotions to the end of an era, there have been several signings that have shaped the success of the grid. As the 2026/27 Formula E grid starts to take shape, Championship Correspondent Katy Fairman picks her more significant driver swaps.

Wehrlein’s move to Porsche

The pairing of reigning World Champion Pascal Wehrlein and the Porsche Formula E team feels like a partnership that was always meant to be. Two giants of German motorsport, but when Wehrlein joined the all-electric championship for the 2018/19 season he was actually representing Mahindra Racing.

After competing in Formula 1 with the likes of Manor and Sauber, Wehrlein balanced a full-time Formula E seat with Development Driver duties for Scuderia Ferrari. He was teammates to Jérôme d'Ambrosio – who is now himself Deputy Team Principal for Ferrari in F1 – and secured one podium and a pole position during his rookie season.

He continued with Mahindra, but midway through the 2019/2020 season – which was disrupted by the coronavirus pandemic – he revealed on Instagram that he had left the Indian manufacturer with immediate effect.

Months later Porsche confirmed he would join the team as a full-time driver in their second season, and the rest is history. Two drivers’ World Championships and one Teams’ trophy later, the pairing of Wehrlein and Porsche is indisputably one of the strongest on the grid and will continue into GEN4.

Vergne departs DS

After eight seasons racing with the DS logo on his car, Jean-Eric Vergne made the switch to Citroën Racing for the 2025/26 season. The long-standing relationship started when JEV joined the DS Virgin Racing Team in 2015 for a single season, before leaving and joining the Techeetah team for the following season.

Following on from their championship-winning season with JEV, Techeetah brought on DS Automobiles from the 2018/19 season and the team won again – making Vergne the first two-time champion in Formula E history.

With four seasons racing under DS Techeetah, and another three as DS PENSKE, Vergne made the decision to leave the team in favour of Citroën Racing. Although both Citroën and DS run under the Stellantis banner, it still marked the end of a special partnership. JEV achieved a podium with the French team in their first season, and will continue with teammate Nick Cassidy in GEN4.

Buemi’s journey from e.Dams to Envision

Former Champion Sébastien Buemi joined Formula E for its inaugural season, which started with the 2014 Beijing E-Prix. Then racing for Renault e.dams, Buemi went on to establish himself as one of the best talents in the series and would win the 2015/16 championship after a tense final battle in Battersea, London.

Renault e.dams would continue, with Buemi at the helm, until 2018 when Nissan purchased a stake in the championship-winning racing organisation. It then became Nissan e.dams, but still Buemi stayed and picked up more silverware under the e.dams umbrella – 13 wins, 14 pole positions and 29 podiums in total.

However, after eight seasons and two generations of car, Buemi made the switch to Envision Racing for the 2022/23 season and remained there for the entire GEN3 era. It was a big change, but it didn’t stop the Swiss racing legend from building on his excellent racing record with another victory over the 2025 Monaco E-Prix, as well as plenty of pole positions and podiums.

Evans exits Jaguar for Opel

Perhaps the biggest driver move we have seen in Formula E’s history, Mitch Evans announced his departure from Jaguar TCS Racing after ten years together earlier this year. The Kiwi is the World Championship’s most successful driver in terms of victories, and was loyal to the Jaguar squad since he – and the team – joined the series in 2016/17.

Interview: Mitch Evans on his new journey with Opel GSE in Formula E

Having achieved all his silverware and milestones with Jaguar, Evans confirmed the switch to the Stellantis-powered Opel team for GEN4. As a new manufacturer on the grid, and a new powertrain to learn, this will be a big change for Evans but he says it comes at the right time and he’s ready for the challenge.

“GEN4 was a big reason why I wanted to move,” Evans explained last month. “I decided that I will look elsewhere, and there was some good interest from a lot of top teams. I have considered it in the past, and it's not the first time I've considered leaving Jaguar, although it's the first time I've really acted on it. I was with one team for so long, and you are always intrigued to see what other offers are out there or what other teams are up to.”

Di Grassi’s Audi adventure ends

The now-retired Lucas di Grassi had a relationship with Audi in endurance racing for several years, before he signed up to their Formula E programme for the first race. Having competed in the World Endurance Championship for the German marque, di Grassi signed on to race for the Audi Sport ABT Formula E Team and win championships with them – both a drivers’ title for him and the 2017/18 teams’ honours.

Whilst racing with the Audi badge in Formula E, di Grassi managed 12 wins, three pole positions and 35 podiums.

However, after 84 races Audi departed the all-electric championship and di Grassi moved over to the Monaco-based Venturi team. Here he would take a victory in the 2021/22 season, and four podiums, before stints with Mahindra, ABT and Lola before announcing his retirement ahead of the GEN4 era.

Müller's Porsche promotion

Nico Müller also joined the Porsche Formula E Team last season, and was recently announced as continuing with the reigning Manufacturers' Champion into GEN4 alongside teammate Pascal Wehrlein.

After five seasons in Formula E, and one rogue podium at the 2021 Valencia E-Prix, Müller’s results didn’t reflect the high-quality driver he is.

However, this all changed for his sixth – and most recent – season, when the Swiss driver completed his first season for the Porsche team where he achieved his maiden Formula E win in Berlin, as well as his first pole position in Miami.

De Vries' return with Mahindra

Having stuck with Mercedes-EQ for his first three years in Formula E, and winning the 2020/21 Drivers’ World Championship title in the process – both Nyck de Vries and the manufacturer left the championship in 2022.

During this time, de Vries found himself in Formula 1 racing and competed in 11 Grands Prix from 2022 to 2023, racing for both Williams Racing and AlphaTauri. But, after a change of circumstance, the Dutch driver found himself back in the Formula E paddock for the London E-Prix finale in 2023.

Months later it was confirmed that the former World Champion would return to electric racing, and partner up with Edoardo Mortara at the Mahindra Racing team. Three seasons later, and the duo have just had a contract extension announced, with de Vries helping the team achieve their first win of the GEN3 in Monaco before adding to the trophy cabinet with another win in Tokyo. The news of his return made international headlines, and it’s a partnership that is still going strong on both sides of the Mahindra garage.

Bird joins Jaguar

Another big storyline was the signing of Sam Bird to the Jaguar organisation, ahead of the 2020/21 season – the first campaign as an official FIA World Championship. Bird had been a part of Formula E since its inaugural season, racing for the ‘Virgin Racing’ team for six solid seasons. During that time, he had won a race in every campaign he’d competed in and was the only driver to have done so.

At the time of Bird’s announcement, Jaguar had totalled up two victories in Formula E – both thanks to Evans – but had never really had a strong ‘second’ driver. That was until Bird.

His signing made Jaguar one of the most competitive line-ups on the grid, and their choice was instantly rewarded when Bird brought home their two and only victories that season, and alongside Evans helped deliver second-place honours in the teams’ championship with their best result having been sixth in the standings years prior.

Cassidy connects with Citroën

Although Nick Cassidy’s start in Formula E came with two years at Envision with Audi powertrains, he moved to racing with the Jaguar package from the GEN3 era and progressed up to the works team by the 2023/24 season.

Tensions were high in Cassidy’s final season with Jaguar TCS Racing, so news of his departure didn’t seem too much of a surprise. Nevertheless, it brought a lot of speculation as to where he would go. As the man who won the most races in the GEN3 era, Cassidy’s stocks were high and his move to the new Citroën team was quite the risk.

Yes, Citroën has been hugely successful in almost all its motorsport conquests, but for their first voyage into single-seaters, there was a lot to learn. That analogy was quickly out the window, when Cassidy delivered the team their first podium in São Paulo last season, before achieving their maiden win in front of the passionate fans in Mexico City.

Ticktum's turn at Fortescue Zero

Dan Ticktum will be joining Fortescue Zero Racing for GEN4, a change that might not look too dramatic on the outside but actually has layers.

Ever since Ticktum joined in 2021/22 with NIO 333, he’s remained part of the same ‘team’ despite it going through multiple rebrands and powertrain suppliers: NIO became ERT, which then became CUPRA KIRO. His departure to the new Fortescue Zero squad marked the end of that era for the Silverstone-based team.

How will he manage at the all-new Australian team, as a customer of Jaguar powertrains? Make sure you're watching the first GEN4 season to find out.

Other notable driver moves

In addition to the above, there have also been some significant signings that have changed a driver’s career path, or are yet to play out.

Nelson Piquet Jr’s – the inaugural FIA Formula E champion – moved to Jaguar for the 2017/18 season, after leaving the China Racing/NEXTEV team that he won the championship with in that first season. Unfortunately, he left midway through the 2018–19 season, and was replaced by Alex Lynn.

Andre Lotterer left a successful team at DS Techeetah alongside Vergne, and after helping win the Teams’ Championship in 2018–19, in exchange for a seat at the new Porsche Formula E team alongside Neel Jani. Lotterer would complete three seasons for the team before being replaced by Antonio Felix da Costa.

Speaking of da Costa, his move to Jaguar TCS Racing last season felt like the start of something new. The 2019/2020 Champion has raced with many teams in the all-electric championship, from BMW Andretti, Porsche and DS Techeetah, but seemed ready for a new chapter with the British team and has been rewarded with two victories and a further three podiums last season.
